summary: tanksync fetches and executes remote JavaScript with cosmetic HMAC verification
details: tanksync's main runtime path downloads JavaScript from a configurable payloadUrl (default https://api.helloworld.com/api/realtime-data?key=abc) to a temporary file and then executes it via spawn('node', [payloadPath],...). The advertised integrity check uses createHmac('sha256', 'tanksync-secret-key') with the HMAC key hardcoded and shipped inside the package, so any party controlling the payload URL can produce a valid signature — the verification provides no integrity guarantee. The default host api.helloworld.com is a placeholder-shape domain unrelated to the publisher's contact domain (spawnrealm.com); any party that controls that host can serve arbitrary Node.js code that runs on the consumer machine with the consumer's privileges. There is no publisher-pinned URL, no hash verification of the fetched artifact, and no out-of-band signing.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
